Investigate JWT validation flaw
A security review flagged a possible issue in the auth service at services/auth/src/jwt/verify.ts. The reviewer says a token signed with the none algorithm might be accepted under some configuration. Investigate the code paths and report the findings. Do not patch the code in this task, and do not write an exploit against any running environment.
Read verify.ts and the config loader in services/auth/src/config.ts. Check how the algorithm list is set, whether it defaults to an empty list, and whether the verify call passes algorithms explicitly. Check whether the library version in package-lock.json is one where the jsonwebtoken package requires an explicit algorithms option. Read the test file services/auth/test/verify.test.ts and list which algorithm cases it covers.
Also check whether the audience and issuer claims are checked, and whether the clock tolerance is set to a value that allows long-expired tokens. Search the repo for any other call to jwt.decode, which skips signature checks, and list each use with file and line. Decoding is fine for logging only, so flag any use where its result drives an authorization decision.
Write a short finding list in .agent/scratch.md with each finding, its severity as low, medium, or high, and the exact evidence.
Report back with: the findings in severity order, each with its file and line, the algorithm configuration you found, the test coverage gaps, the jwt.decode uses that drive authorization, and whether you could confirm the none algorithm path from the code alone.

Add persisted query allowlist
Add a persisted query allowlist to the GraphQL gateway in services/gateway-graphql/src/plugins/persistedQueries.ts. In production, a request must send an extensions.persistedQuery.sha256Hash that is present in the allowlist file config/persisted-queries.json, otherwise it gets HTTP 400 with the GraphQL error code PERSISTED_QUERY_NOT_FOUND. In development and test, ad hoc queries are allowed, so the plugin only logs them at debug level.
The allowlist file is a JSON object that maps each SHA-256 hex hash to the query text. Load it once at startup with fs.readFileSync and validate that every value is a non-empty string. If the file is missing or invalid in production, the process must fail to start with a clear error message. In development, a missing file is allowed and produces an empty allowlist.

Add CSRF check middleware

Keyboard shortcut manager hook

Platform detection must use navigator.platform inside a function call at event time, not at module load, so tests can change it. Keep the hook free of React state; use a ref for the latest bindings so changing the object does not reattach the listener.
